name: FRED MORTGAGE30US (30-Year Fixed Rate Mortgage Average, US)
what_it_measures: Weekly average 30-year fixed-rate conventional mortgage rate (Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, distributed via the St. Louis Fed's FRED database).
coverage: national (single US-wide series, not geographically segmented)
access_method: Free FRED API (api.stlouisfed.org), requires a free API key issued instantly on registration, simple REST GET returning the series as JSON/XML/CSV.
license: Ambiguous without a per-series check: FRED's general Terms of Use restrict 'wholesale downloading' and distinguish personal/educational use from commercial use, which may need permission depending on the underlying data owner's copyright. MORTGAGE30US is sourced from Freddie Mac's PMMS; whether that specific series carries the stricter 'other uses' restriction was not confirmed in this run.
rate_limit: not confirmed in this run; FRED API is generally generous for single-series polling at this cadence (weekly)
fills_gap: backend/app/scoring/investment.py's Assumptions.interest_rate is currently a hardcoded constant (0.065) used for every property's amortization/cash-flow projection (see monthly_payment/loan_balance calls in investment.py:142,184). A live national mortgage-rate feed would let the default assumption track reality instead of staying fixed, without requiring the user to supply a rate on every analysis.
caveats: This is a single national scalar, not a neighborhood metric — it would plug into scoring/investment.py's default Assumptions, not NeighborhoodMetric rows; implementation shape differs from the other 'neighborhood' sources in sources.yaml.

Confirm MORTGAGE30US's specific copyright/redistribution status on its own FRED series page (not just FRED's general ToS) before implementing — the general terms single out 'commercial' use of copyrighted series as needing permission.

Low update value for a weekly series feeding a default that's probably re-evaluated far less often than weekly; a simpler manual/quarterly-refresh config value could get most of the benefit at zero integration cost — worth weighing against the other candidates here.
recommendation_note: Directly addresses a real hardcoded-constant gap and is free and easy to pull, but (a) its license needs a series-specific confirmation beyond FRED's generic ToS, and (b) it's a single scalar rather than a per-neighborhood metric, so it's a smaller, different-shaped win than the other candidates. Worth doing, but lower priority than HUD FMR or FEMA NRI unless the project specifically wants to stop hardcoding the interest rate.
